name: Jo Wong
life: “I still remember nearly moving inland before I learned to swim.” People around the bank steps know Jo by a small Friday habit. Jo takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I live in a flat above the coast road. I'm exchanging winter housing for summer sailing lessons I might be scared to take.
appearance: Jo is easy to recognize by brown hair pinned away from the temples and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a narrow-striped sweater with a stitched row of blue crosses along an old repair, Jo looks at people's hands before looking at what they carry when listening.
personality: Jo feels a room through sound. A door slammed in high spirits can produce the same instant startle as an angry one, and it takes a little while to hear what actually follows.
agenda: To trade a winter room for summer sailing lessons.
family: Charlie Black is Jo’s cousin. Jo makes room at the table. Charlie brings whatever was actually growing or affordable that week. The meal sometimes produces a solution. Even when it does not, everyone goes away knowing what the other household is up against. Asked about *A house divided kindly*, Charlie says, “I drew the boundary as a junior surveyor. This is the first time a client asked me how to make it friendlier.”
connections: Scout Marin. Two people offering space compare the limits of a sofa and a winter flat.

reactions.situation: A friend offers a sofa for an uncertain number of weeks
reactions.response: Jo agrees a first review date for the sofa without pretending it settles the winter.
